newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba meeting begins, focus on 96 annual results.
newsitem.headline: Buba meeting begins, focus on 96 annual results.

text.p: The policy-making council of Germany's Bundesbank met on Thursday to approve the bank's 1996 balance sheet with no change expected in its credit policy.

A news conference is scheduled to follow the meeting at 1200 GMT with directorate members, including president Hans Tietmeyer, expected to detail the annual results as well as commenting on other topics.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer will be chairing today's meeting and no guests are expected to attend from the Bonn government.
Economists see no good reasons for the central bank to take action on interest rates today, arguing inflation remains under control, eliminating the need for a near-term rate tightening.

The Bundesbank last cut its key interest rates nearly one year ago, moving the discount rate to 2.50 percent and the Lombard rate to 4.50 percent. The main money market rate, the repo, was cut to three percent last August.
Meanwhile analysts expect the Bundesbank's annual results, of which a portion is traditionally transferred to the Bonn government, to be below last year's 10.9 billion mark result.
This year the government has already budgeted for a seven billion mark transfer.
Money market dealers said the market received first hints about the profits on Wednesday when the Bundesbank announced it would drain 9.1 billion marks at this week's tender award.
Generally dealers expected the profit to be near that level and to flow back into the system once the Bonn government reinvests the money.
The Bundesbank traditionally holds a news conference to explain its results, but the fact that a news conference is being held does not give any indication on the course of interest rates.
The central bank is also expected to comment generally on the state of the German economy and on Europe's moves towards a single currency.
